discovery: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene: prediction and discovery of flat-band correlated insulators and superconductivity in moire materials

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and correlated electrons
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so that interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group fabricated such devices with a precise tear-and-stack method and found correlated insulating states and superconductivity, which could be tuned by a gate voltage in a single device. The twist angle became a new control parameter for quantum matter. It gave rise to the field of moire materials, in which correlated insulators, orbital magnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and, more recently, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states have been observed in clean, gate-tunable two-dimensional crystals. Few discoveries have opened such a fertile experimental platform so quickly. The prediction was simple, the device engineering was ingenious and the transport data were unambiguous. The discovery has transformed how we search for strongly correlated and topological phases.
